fixes.explanation: Signs it is. Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a leader of the Jews, says, “For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.” He's telling Jesus what he has noticed and what he thinks it means. I think the man had a lot on his mind before he ever came to Jesus.

Nicodemus never says a word about sacrifices. He says, “For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.” The signs are what he says Jesus is doing. Sacrifices belong to a whole different conversation, friend.

Going back to your hometown sounds like a fine weekend trip, but it's not what Nicodemus asks about. He says, “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?” That's the picture he gives. No hometown anywhere in that question.
Amazed is right. Jesus says, “Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’” He says it right after talking about being born of the Spirit. I think a little amazement is understandable.
The text doesn't say Nicodemus was angry. Jesus tells him, “Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’” The word Jesus uses is amazed. Angry just isn't in the verse, friend.

Yes, you hear it. Jesus says, “You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going.” The sound shows up even when the rest stays a mystery. It's like hearing the oven timer from the other room and still having no idea who set it.

True. Jesus says the wind blows where it wishes, then adds, “So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” The wind is His picture for them. Nicodemus had just asked about being born, and this is the picture Jesus gives next.
It's the other way around. Jesus says, “…and yet you people do not accept our testimony.” That's a real moment of honesty in the conversation. So they don't accept it, friend.

Yes, the Son of Man. Jesus says, “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up…” Moses is the one who lifted the snake. And Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

The temple isn't what Jesus mentions. He says, “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up…” Moses lifted the snake. Jesus pairs it with the Son of Man, which is the name He uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

Moses is in the sentence, but his law isn't. Jesus says, “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up…” Moses is the one who lifted the snake. Jesus is the Son of Man, the name He uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

It's true, and it's a tough one. Jesus says, “…whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.” Those are His words. So True is the answer here.

Waiting for a bigger sign isn't in this verse. Jesus says, “The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light…” That's the response He names. A greater sign isn't part of it.

That's the reason. Jesus says, “Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.” The fear is about what the Light would show. I think that's a heavy thing to carry around.
It's the opposite. Jesus says, “But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light…” That's who walks toward it. So they don't stay away, friend.

Right, False. Jesus says, “But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.” They come toward the Light and don't stay away. I think that's a beautiful verse.
